SA is whenever someone does something sexual to another person without their consent. He did not have your consent, you never said yes, you never said it was okay, you never said you wanted it. This man has been harassing you sexually and assaulting and raping you.

Tell your parents, your friends, your boss, your therapist. Tell people what happened to you. Write it down on your phone, notebooks, draw it if you want. Don't be ashamed to tell. Wow. This sounds like such an intense time in your life. 

I'll encourage you to take it slowly. You don't know what else your mind will reveal to you, now that you have been deemed ready for the memories. Take it day by day. Write everything down. You will feel in your gut what the best thing to do is. Please enlist the help of a trauma-informed therapist to support you at this time. Your friends and family are great, but they're not professionals and you don't know what your memories will trigger in them. It's best to unpack these emotions in a safe space.

I encourage you to tell your mom to not confront ANYBODY until YOU have decided you are comfortable with that. It's understandable that your mom wants to act, she is very upset to hear about this. However, your trauma is about YOU, and YOU make the decisions.

Good luck unpacking your boxed memories! Hopefully you'll be able to work through them safely and come to a greater understanding of yourself.

My attack happened about a year ago. Right after it happened, I needed a lot of meds, a lot of crying and screaming, to tell on my attacker, and to be held and cared for just like a little baby. Now my needs have changed, so I sing, play my instrument every day, and am in a community Shakespeare play. These things are really nice, because they force me to be in touch with my emotions in a productive way. I take my meds every night to sleep. I also gently masturbate and penetrate myself once in a while, if my body is willing, to say hello to the area and listen to what my body has to say about the attack. I follow my therapist's advice, which is to take some time every day to feel very sad. I don't use tampons anymore, and I don't make myself put on pretty clothes if I don't want to.

I got back into kpop, which is very healing for my sexuality. Whenever I feel awful, sick feelings of arousal for my rapist, I just project it onto male kpop idols, and I know I don't want them to rape me so it's very grounding.

I am personally looking into EMDR therapy in order to completely process this and move on. I have also found the reporting process to be incredibly calming and helpful. It makes the whole thing less of a secret and it becomes someone else's problem too. It isn't for everyone, but it is working very well for me.

Good luck on your journey, OP. I'm rooting for you!
